desc: Formalize the correct equivalence: strong connectivity iff every adjacent cut k has at least one backward pair (b,w) with b≤k<w; note forward W→B edges with w<b are redundant and the graph need not be one 2N-cycle.
Derive necessary quick-zero conditions from the cut criterion/online state: S_1 must be B, S_{2N} must be W, and no proper prefix may contain all N whites while having nonnegative W−B balance.

Build the online matching DP: scan prefixes, track x=#seen blacks still unmatched to future whites and D=#W−#B; show validity is simply x_i≥1 for every proper prefix and x_{2N}=0, with y=x+D pending whites.
Specify exact transitions and weights for W/B steps (match to pending black/white vs leave pending), prove each perfect matching is generated once, and identify why naive O(N^2) is too slow.

Brute-force tiny N in analysis to validate the cut criterion and DP against exhaustive pairing and edge cases (B^N W^N → N!, W^N B^N → 0, alternating cases), without putting sample tests in final code.

Derive a near-linear simplification of the exact DP: scan with bal=#B−#W and minbal; first B and last W forced; for each non-final W multiply by bal−minbal; require final bal==1 and minbal==-1; O(N) time/O(1) space.
Validate the simplified formula against the brute force/cut-cover/DP checks on structured families and edge cases.
